gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 28?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 28 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from multiple sources converge on a daytime peak near 29°C for Munich on August 28, driven by southwesterly flow and modest daytime heating under partly cloudy skies, with afternoon scattered thunderstorms likely to increase cloud cover and limit further warming through evaporative cooling and reduced insolation. This places the outcome near or slightly above the long-term average high of 22.9°C while well below the August 28 record of 32.5°C. Market-implied odds clustering around 29–31°C reflect trader weighting of ensemble uncertainty in storm timing and intensity, which can shift the exact maximum by 1–2°C depending on whether convection develops before or after peak solar heating. Updated short-range guidance expected overnight will refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus points to a high of 23–25°C in Munich on August 29, 2026, as a cooler maritime air mass arrives from the west behind a weakening frontal system.** Multiple models, including ECMWF, ICON, and GFS runs valid as of August 27, show daytime maxima near 23–24°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies with light westerly flow and a modest chance of showers, limiting afternoon insolation compared with the warmer, sunnier conditions of August 27–28. This matches the historical late-August average high of ~22.8°C and explains why 24°C and 25°C together command roughly 72% of the market-implied probability.

**Key differentiating factors among the tightly bunched outcomes include the precise timing and extent of cloud cover and any embedded showers, which can suppress the daily maximum by 1–3°C.** Stronger or more persistent cloud decks, or earlier arrival of the cooler advection, favor the lower side (23–24°C), while brief clearing or slightly delayed frontal timing could allow brief peaks near 25–26°C. Ensemble spread remains modest at this 48-hour lead time, but small differences in boundary-layer moisture and wind direction near the Alps can shift the realized high within that narrow range. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance over the next 24 hours will provide the clearest signals ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from the National Weather Service and private sources converge on a highest temperature near 82–84°F for New York City on August 28, 2026, consistent with the market’s top outcomes (82–83°F at 43.5%, 80–81°F at 23.5%, and 84–85°F at 22.5%).** Normal August highs average 82°F at Central Park, so today’s expected range sits close to climatology but with modest upward or downward variance driven by cloud cover and convection.

Key scientific drivers include a post-frontal airmass with west-to-northwest flow, reduced humidity after overnight clearing, and afternoon instability that supports a 30–40% chance of showers or thunderstorms. These storms can cap temperatures by limiting solar heating or allow brief spikes if they hold off until late in the day. Model consensus shows highs in the low-to-mid 80s across Central Park, LaGuardia, and JFK, with little spread between guidance runs issued late on August 27.

Recent developments reinforce this positioning: widespread severe thunderstorms on August 27 brought heavy rain and gusty winds that moistened the boundary layer but also cleared skies overnight, setting up partly sunny conditions for the 28th. No major heat ridge or tropical moisture plume is present to push values into the upper 80s or higher, keeping the probability of 86°F+ below 10%. Traders appear to weight the official NWS point forecasts and ensemble means most heavily, producing tight clustering around the 80–85°F bins while assigning negligible odds to extremes outside historical late-August variability.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast updates from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency and international models indicate Tokyo will see increased cloud cover, scattered rain, and northeasterly flow on August 29, limiting daytime heating and supporting a maximum near 27–28°C. This follows hotter conditions earlier in the week, with ensemble guidance showing modest cooling from persistent moisture and reduced insolation rather than clear skies that could push readings toward 30°C or above. Historical climatology for late August favors highs near 31°C, but the current pattern aligns more closely with the lower end of recent runs, where model spread centers on the 26–29°C range. Traders are weighting the latest deterministic outputs and ensemble probabilities, which emphasize uncertainty around exact peak timing amid variable precipitation. Further model updates and official JMA briefings in the next 24 hours will refine these odds before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the UK Met Office and European models point to a maximum of 20–22°C in London on August 29 under cloudy skies with periods of light rain and moderate southwesterly winds. These conditions, driven by an approaching Atlantic low-pressure system, suppress daytime heating and keep readings close to the late-August climatological average of roughly 21°C. Trader consensus, reflected in the 43.5% implied probability for 21°C and 25.5% for 20°C, aligns with this narrow forecast range, while lower odds for 22°C or higher reflect model agreement on limited insolation and potential for heavier showers. Updated guidance ahead of the 29th will be key for any shifts in these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current National Weather Service and NOAA model guidance for New York City on August 29 points to a daily maximum in the upper 70s to low 80s, with ensemble spreads creating the tight market clustering around 78–83 °F. Key differentiating factors include variable afternoon cloud cover, boundary-layer moisture, and the strength of any onshore flow or weak frontal passage that could cap heating or enhance mixing. Late-August climatology shows a historical average high near 82 °F, yet recent model runs have trended slightly cooler, reflecting modest uncertainty in insolation and wind patterns. Traders are weighting the most probable range where forecast confidence is highest while discounting outliers beyond 84 °F that would require stronger high-pressure building or clearer skies than currently indicated.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency and other models points to a Tokyo high of 31–32°C on August 28, 2026, aligning with the market's heaviest weighting on those outcomes.** 

Cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers, driven by lingering summer monsoon moisture and southeasterly flow, are limiting daytime heating and keeping temperatures near the late-August climatological normal of ~30°C. Current observations show morning readings near 28–30°C under mostly cloudy conditions, with model runs indicating modest afternoon peaks unlikely to exceed 33°C absent a significant break in cloud cover. Recent forecast updates from August 27 have reinforced this moderate range rather than signaling intensification or suppression, supporting trader consensus around the 31–33°C band while assigning low probability to outliers above 34°C or below 31°C.

Typical late-August climatology for Central Park places the average daily maximum near 82°F, but the incoming high-pressure ridge and light winds (5–10 mph) limit further warming while clear conditions allow efficient daytime heating.

The tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 78–81°F therefore reflects this narrow but still unresolved range, with lower odds on 82–83°F (16%) and minimal pricing for extremes above 84°F. **Forecast models and observational data indicate a peak temperature in Munich on August 28, 2026, most likely in the 29–31°C range, aligning closely with the market-implied probabilities (30°C at 46%, 31°C at 20.5%, 29°C at 19%).** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug (high near 29°C/85°F), Met Office (28°C), and others projecting 27–30°C, reflect warm air advection under partly cloudy skies early in the day, with daytime highs supported by solar heating before afternoon instability develops.

Key scientific drivers include moderate northwest winds, dew points around 15–18°C promoting efficient heating, and a frontal boundary or trough triggering scattered thunderstorms by midday or afternoon. These convective events—often linked to 50–80% precipitation probabilities in forecasts—increase cloud cover, enhance evaporative cooling, and disrupt surface heating, typically capping the daily maximum below the historical record of 32.5°C. Early observations on the day show temperatures climbing from ~18°C at dawn toward 26–28°C by midday, consistent with this trajectory.

Trader consensus, reflected in the tight clustering around 29–31°C, incorporates the latest model consensus (GFS/ECMWF runs) and real-time station data from Munich International Airport, where skin-in-the-game incentives favor accurate assessment of these meteorological thresholds over climatological averages (~23°C). Upcoming afternoon observations and any revised short-range forecasts could further refine resolution as storms evolve.
